content:
- Model consistently underestimates true prices, especially in the first 10–15 days of the forecast horizon.
- Overshoots after sharp upward spikes in history (e.g., 44.49 → 45.13, 45.93 → 45.93), then fails to correct downward.
- Underestimates mean-reverting periods — fails to recognize when prices are near historical highs and should decline.
- Overreacts to recent volatility — forecasts too much downward correction after spikes, then misses upward rebounds.
- Lags in response to new data — true values often exceed forecasted values by 1–3 days, suggesting model is slow to adjust to new information.
- Overly conservative in early forecast days — especially for 30-day horizons, model starts low and doesn’t rise as fast as true values.
- Fails to capture tail risk — underestimates extreme upward moves (e.g., 47.20, 48.22) and overestimates downward moves (e.g., 33.70, 33.16) in volatile periods.
